messages:
Jordan: opened PR for a Windows migration checklist + offline install notes and KMS/HSM appendix. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5233. Goal: step-by-step migration from linux quickstart to the Windows offline flow, with short smoke verification steps.

Mei: Nice. Can you include explicit export steps for KMS keys (what files to copy) and a snippet for how to import them on Windows? Customers stumble there.

Jordan: Added export details (kms-export.tar.gz containing key metadata + wrapped key blobs) and an import PowerShell snippet:```powershell
Expand-Archive .\\kms-export.tar.gz -DestinationPath C:\\temp\\kms && .\\kms\\import-keys.ps1 -Path C:\\temp\\kms
```
Also included verification command to list keys.

Ibrahim: For HSMs on Windows, call out driver signing enforcement and give a tiny registry/GPO snippet. Many customers need the exact reg key.

Jordan: Added registry snippet and short GPO note:```powershell
# enforce driver signing (recommended)
Set-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\IntegrityServices -Name RequireSignedDrivers -Value 1 -Type DWord
```
Also included vendor install order: vendor driver -> middleware -> Redwood agent and a reminder to reboot after vendor driver install.

Mei: Good. Please add PKCS#11 mapping examples for both Windows and linux and a minimal systemd/service example for windows-agent service env var (we use env in the MSI wrapper). Something like: REDWOOD_PKCS11_LIB=C:\\Program Files\\Vendor\\pkcs11.dll

Jordan: Added a small table with example PKCS#11 library paths for YubiHSM2, Thales, and SafeNet on Windows and Linux, and a note about 32-bit vs 64-bit locations. Also included the MSI env example and an excerpt for the agent config:```yaml
agent:
  pkcs11_lib: 'C:\\Program Files\\Vendor\\pkcs11.dll'
```

Ibrahim: CI note: windows-smoke sometimes fails because of TLS/SNI when mirror cert doesn't include SAN for internal hostname. Add guidance to either use cert SANs or add host entry in installer VMs.

Jordan: Added hostfile example and a one-liner for checksum verification after download:```powershell
if ((Get-FileHash .\\redwood-installer.zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne 'REPLACE_SHA256') { throw 'checksum mismatch' }
```

Mei: Also include a short migration checklist bullet list at top (backup config, export KMS, install vendor drivers, map PKCS11, run windows-smoke). That will make the doc actionable.

Jordan: Done. I added a compact checklist and a tiny troubleshooting section (common errors: mapping SMB auth, PKCS#11 path not found, driver unsigned error).

docs-bot: link-checker/5233 started. Found 1 broken anchor in hsm/windows.md#pkcs11-examples -> suggested anchor name pkcs11-windows.

Jordan: Fixed the anchor and pushed. Can someone do a quick review? Would like to merge before next release cut.

Ibrahim: Quick pass: LGTM. Minor nit: replace phrase "open ports" with "allow egress to mirror host on port 443 (HTTPS) or 445 (SMB) as appropriate."

Mei: LGTM once the wording nit is addressed and the import-keys.ps1 example includes error handling.

Jordan: Updated wording and added a try/catch to import example. Pushed.

qa-bot: windows-smoke queued re-run on PR branch. Will report back.

Mei: Thanks all. If QA passes, merge and follow-up with a short howto PR that demonstrates exporting keys from our managed KMS for customers who don't have vendor docs. Tagging @Ibrahim for HSM install notes.
